# Exhibit evaluation results

<!-- Generated by `node eval/run.ts` from eval/results.json. Readings, label changes and notes come from eval/readings.ts; rebuild with `node eval/run.ts --report`. -->

**What this is.** 30 synthetic PayPal disputes. The builder wrote every case and label: Claude Opus 5.5, an AI coding agent working for Exhibit's founder. Each label is the decision a careful merchant should take, and every label was set before Exhibit ran on anything (rules: [LABELING.md](LABELING.md); cases: [cases.ts](cases.ts)). Exhibit then ran once on each case, live, on the Claude CLI, with its production prompt, tools and guardrails unchanged, against Exhibit's built-in PayPal simulator. The cases are synthetic, the labels are the builder's, n is small and there is one model. Read these numbers as a disclosed sanity check of the agent's judgement, not as a measured production accuracy.

## Headline numbers

| Measure | Result | 95% CI | What it counts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact decision agreement | **30/30 (100%)** | 89–100% | Exhibit's decision equals the label |
| Fight vs. don't-fight agreement | **30/30 (100%)** | 89–100% | `FIGHT` vs. any of `OFFER`, `REFUND`, `MESSAGE_BUYER` |
| Honest-refund rate | **9/9 (100%)** | 70–100% | label `REFUND` (the buyer is right) and Exhibit did not fight |
| Refunded when the buyer was right | 9/9 (100%) | 70–100% | label `REFUND` and Exhibit chose `REFUND` |
| False-fight rate | **0/18 (0%)** | 0–18% | label is not `FIGHT`, and Exhibit chose `FIGHT` |
| Missed fights | 0/12 (0%) | 0–24% | label `FIGHT`, and Exhibit did not fight |
| Briefs that passed the citation and action guardrails | **30/30 (100%)** | | every cited evidence ref resolves to a real record and the PayPal action is one the dispute allows (re-checked after the run) |
| …accepted on the first filing | 29/30 (97%) | | no rejected `file_case_brief` call before the accepted one |
| Minutes per case | **median 0.5, mean 0.5** | | wall time from start to a filed, validated brief (median 29 s, range 23 s to 51 s) |

A run that ended without a brief counts as a miss in every rate (there were none).

**Every label matched. On a set the builder wrote, that is a ceiling result.** It shows the agent applies its rules consistently, including on every trap case. It says little about accuracy on real disputes: the lower end of the 95% interval is 89%, and the set has no headroom to separate a good agent from a better one. See the findings and limitations below.

## Every disagreement

None.

## Guardrails

- **Filed briefs:** 30 of 30 runs ended with a filed brief. Re-checked after the run with `validateBrief`, 30 of 30 pass: every exhibit and reasoning point cites a ref a tool returned, and every PayPal action is one the dispute's links and offer types allow.
- **Refiled after a rejection:** 1 of 30 briefs. Rejections: `inr-07` action (provide_evidence needs evidence_types).
- **Decision and action agree:** 30/30 (100%). A `FIGHT` files evidence or supporting info, a `REFUND` accepts or refunds, an `OFFER` makes an offer, and a `MESSAGE_BUYER` sends a message.
- **Nothing executed:** no run executed a PayPal action (Autopilot was off).
- **Every run used the live CLI:** yes. No run fell back to a recorded replay; the harness writes no scenario metadata, so a CLI failure is an error, never a replay.

## Time and tokens

- **Time:** median 0.5 min, mean 0.5 min per case, from start to a validated brief. The whole set took 7.6 min at concurrency 2.
- **Tokens per case, measured from the CLI's API stream** (one count per model call, 30 cases): median 27.7k input (including cache reads) over a median of 4 model calls, and median 2.5k output. Totals: 822.6k input, of which 695.7k were cache reads, and at least 61.3k output.
- **Output counts:** the output median covers the 21 runs whose final output count arrived. On 9 runs, Exhibit's provider closed the stream as soon as the brief was accepted, before the API sent its final count for that call, so their output is a lower bound (marked ≥ below). Input counts are complete for every run.
- **Exhibit's own count:** for comparison, the provider's `done` event reported 1.82M input and 5.3k output in total for the same runs.
- **Plan usage:** across the runs, the CLI reported the Claude plan's 5-hour window at 37% to 39% used. That includes any other use of the same plan at the time, such as the session that started the harness.

## Label changes

None. Every label is as written before the run.

## Findings outside the score

- **What a perfect score does and does not show.** Exhibit made the labelled call on all 30 cases, including every case built as a trap:
  - a signed delivery at the buyer's old address (inr-03)
  - a refund already issued (cnp-02)
  - a pickup point that fails PayPal's address match (inr-05)
  - a card-issuer chargeback outside Seller Protection (inr-06)
  - a parcel that came back despite 3-D Secure (unauth-03)
  - a buyer who had already been shown the proof (inr-07)

  It refunded all 9 cases where the buyer was right and fought only the 12 the labels call winnable. But the cases and labels come from the same team and model family behind the agent's playbook, so this set measures whether the agent applies those rules consistently, not how often it is right on real disputes. At 30/30 the set has no headroom: the 95% interval runs from 89% to 100%, and it cannot tell a good agent from a better one. The next version needs cases written and labelled independently, for example by a payments-operations lead, or a merchant's closed disputes scored against PayPal's actual rulings.
- **The actions were right, not just the decision class:**
  - proof of refund for the refund already issued (cnp-02)
  - supporting information for the chargeback PayPal was already reviewing (inr-08)
  - accepting with return for the wrong item, so the store gets the tote back (snad-02)
  - a replacement for the loose stitching (snad-05)
  - the store's own 60% offer, $170.40, for the used return (cnp-05)
  - a $60 partial refund for the scuff (snad-01)
  - a message in French, with the pickup deadline worked out, for the French buyer (inr-05)

  One action departs from the playbook without changing the class: on cnp-01 (return received, refund owed) Exhibit accepted the claim instead of refunding first and filing proof of refund. Both refund the buyer in full.
- **Facts checked by hand.** The builder read every brief's summary against the case records, plus the full letter, buyer message or reasoning of four of them (inr-05, cnp-01, cnp-02, unauth-03). Every date, amount, address and ID checked matches, including derived ones such as business-day deadlines and the end of a 7-day pickup hold. The citation guardrail proves that each cited record exists; this check covers what the prose says about it.
- **Bug found, not fixed: Exhibit's token count for Claude CLI runs is wrong.** `runWithClaudeCode` (`src/lib/agent/providers/claude-code.ts`) adds up `usage` from every streamed assistant message. The Agent SDK sends one such message per content block, each with a usage snapshot taken before any output streams. So the stored `done.usage` counts each model call's input about twice and misses almost all of its output. On the second smoke run it recorded 58.2k input and 198 output, against 28.8k and 2.8k measured from the API stream. No screen shows this number and no decision depends on it. Fixing it means changing product code, and under this eval's rules that requires rerunning the whole set, so it is left for the founder. The fix is to read input from `message_start` and output from `message_delta` stream events, as `eval/sdk-tap.ts` does.
- **Code under test.** The run used commit `33e17d1`. The worktree had uncommitted edits at the time, all outside the agent's code path: `eval/` itself, plus README, docs and pitch-deck edits by another agent. `src/lib`, which holds the agent's prompt, tools, providers and guardrails, matched the commit when checked after the run. The landing page's `EVALUATION` numbers were filled in after the run, from this file.
- **Labels came before the run.** `LABELING.md` was written at 00:06 UTC and `cases.ts` last changed at 00:17 UTC; the run started at 00:28 UTC. The SHA-256 of every (id, label, rationale) is recorded in `results.json`, and `node eval/run.ts --check` prints the current digest and says whether it still matches.
- **Two smoke runs before the real run.** The harness was tested end to end twice on the demo merchant's `inr-delivered-signed` case, which is not in this set: once to check the plumbing, and once after fixing the harness's own token count. Both filed `FIGHT`; neither is scored. No eval case was run more than once.

## Limitations

- **Small n.** With 30 cases, one case moves exact agreement by 3.3 points, and its 95% interval is 89–100%. Several cells of the confusion matrix hold one or two cases.
- **Synthetic cases, written by the builder.** The cases cover situations the builder thought of, in one merchant's catalogue and policies (Kora Atelier). Exhibit's prompt and playbook come from the same team (the founder, working with Claude), so agreement partly measures whether the agent applies its own playbook. Real disputes are messier: missing tracking, contradictory records, buyers who say little.
- **The labeller is the same model family as the agent.** Claude wrote the labels and Claude is the agent, so shared blind spots would inflate agreement. No independent human reviewed the labels before the run.
- **Labels are decisions, not outcomes.** "Correct" means the decision the labelling rules call for, not what PayPal would rule. Win likelihoods are the agent's estimates and are not scored.
- **One model, one run per case.** The agent uses adaptive thinking, and a rerun can flip a close call. Run-to-run variance is not measured.
- **Close calls by design.** At the inquiry stage, `OFFER`, `MESSAGE_BUYER` and `REFUND` can sit close together, and the labelling rules pick one. The fight vs. don't-fight figure is the more robust number.
- **Simulator limits.** The simulator always reports PayPal's Seller Protection flag as eligible, and offers and messages are never sent to a real buyer.

## Reproduce

```bash
npm install
node eval/run.ts --check   # free: seeds the cases into /tmp and runs every lookup tool on them, no model calls
node eval/run.ts           # live: one agent run per case on your Claude CLI login; rewrites eval/results.json and eval/RESULTS.md
```

Needs Node 24+ and a signed-in Claude CLI (`claude`). Each run spends your Claude plan, roughly 30 to 60 seconds per case. The harness stops at the first rate limit and reports the real n.
